name: Enrique Peña Nieto
role: Mexican president (2012–2018); State of Mexico governor (2005–2011)
summary: Peña Nieto promoted competitive markets and private energy investment alongside public resource ownership, social insurance and anti-monopoly regulation. He supported marriage equality, a public-health approach to drug consumption and multilateral cooperation. His security policies and accountability record drew sustained controversy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His governing agreement explicitly sought universal public healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Defended the 2017 increase of 10.4 percent and real wage recovery; larger proposed increases were not adopted.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued that competitive energy markets would improve efficiency and prices.

public-ownership.rationale: Retained PEMEX and public resource ownership, while expressly ending state energy monopolies through private competition.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Advocated progressive taxes with larger contributions from people with greater resources.

unions-good.rationale: Praised workers’ organizations and their constructive role in national development.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Promoted stronger competition regulation and constraints on dominant firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Promoted universal insurance and expanded social protection.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Defended government surveillance technology for internal security and organized-crime investigations, while denying illegal spying on activists.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Favored noncriminalization of consumers and medical cannabis access, while continuing enforcement against illicit supply; this was not blanket legalization.

empower-police-military.rationale: Defended military support for policing and sought a legal framework for it, subject to civilian command and review.

rehabilitation.rationale: Explicitly advocated prison treatment, education, rehabilitation and reintegration, with alternatives to incarceration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Personally proposed constitutional and civil-code recognition of equal marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Personally opposed abortion but said women choosing it should not be criminalized; broader access conditions were unspecified.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His pact recognized historic injustice toward Indigenous peoples and prioritized redress.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His pact committed to protecting archaeological and cultural heritage.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called for strengthening the UN and reforming its Security Council.

free-trade.rationale: Explicitly endorsed free trade and international economic integration.

nation-first.rationale: Rejected exclusionary nationalism and championed international cooperation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Supported binding, verifiable emission-reduction commitments for developed and developing states.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Condemned a return to trade protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed development-bank financing for strategic sectors underserved by commercial banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Praised tripartite institutions and government–employer–worker dialogue over wages and development.

one-party-rule.rationale: Explicitly defended political plurality and cross-party agreement as strengths of democratic government.

democracy-best.rationale: Committed to improving democracy through political plurality and effective institutions.

separate-church-state.rationale: Affirmed a secular state protecting freedom of belief.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Urged retaining effective drug policies and changing approaches that had failed.

direct-action.rationale: Pursued national change through negotiated legislation and institutional reforms.

class-collaboration.rationale: Explicitly favored cooperation and mutual respect between employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: His pact pledged preservation and renewal of inherited cultural institutions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Personally promoted further hydrocarbon extraction auctions, including deepwater deposits.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Promised abuse investigations, yet defended Atenco and the disputed Ayotzinapa account; the record of accountability is mixed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Explicitly demanded equal legal rights without discrimination, including sex and sexual orientation.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His pact expressly maintained secular public education.

separated-powers.rationale: Promised judicial independence and separation of powers, and accepted judicial review of security legislation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His pact prioritized hunger eradication and marginalized communities.

minority-language-support.rationale: His pact explicitly supported bilingual Indigenous education and legal translation.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Called for total nuclear disarmament and universal adherence to the prohibition treaty.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Explicitly favored progressive contributions rather than identical rates across incomes.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Accepted constitutional judicial review of his security policy.

ban-cartels.rationale: His pact empowered competition regulators to break up monopolies.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Explicitly welcomed Supreme Court review and withheld security declarations pending its judgment.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Supported military internal-security operations, while describing their role as temporary and subordinate to civilian authorities.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Welcomed domestic and foreign private entry into strategic energy production; national resource ownership remained.

non-intervention.rationale: Advocated peaceful, locally agreed democratic solutions with full respect for nonintervention; also supported UN peacekeeping.

public-access-to-information.rationale: His pact promised access to public-spending information and an autonomous transparency body.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Proposed consular birth-certificate changes and ordered acceptance of gender-change documents for passports.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combined competitive markets, social insurance and anti-monopoly rules.

independent-unions.rationale: His labor-justice initiative expressly protected union autonomy and freedom of association.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Endorsed carbon pricing and fuel taxes based on carbon content to reduce emissions.

future-generations.rationale: Explicitly described environmental preservation as a responsibility to present and future generations.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: His pact proposed legal limits on subnational debt.

farm-price-support.rationale: His pact offered farmers preferential credit and reoriented subsidies.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Demanded elimination of nuclear weapons, without exempting states facing nuclear rivals.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: His telecom initiative allowed security-related signal blocking; the enacted language was narrowed to stopping crimes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Combined universal insurance with subsidies targeted away from affluent recipients.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Built his reform program through agreements among parties and organized social actors.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Called for removing regressive exemptions and tax privileges.

national-resource-control.rationale: Explicitly retained national ownership of underground hydrocarbons while admitting private and foreign operators.

notes: No inferred answers. Whole-career review includes governorship, the 2012 governing pact, structural reforms, later presidential positions and the 2025 Pegasus denial. The pact is used as a program he personally negotiated and publicly promoted, not as automatic attribution of his party’s doctrine. His energy opening did not abolish public ownership of PEMEX or the hydrocarbon resource. Drug decriminalization, medical use and anti-trafficking enforcement are distinguished from a legal recreational market. Religious personal opposition does not override his stated opposition to criminalizing women who abort. Atenco, Ayotzinapa, military policing, Pegasus and the earlier transparency veto were reviewed; allegations and opponents’ descriptions do not establish that he personally approved every abuse. His support for surveillance is tied to his own security justification, with illegality explicitly denied. Binding climate commitments coexist with fossil-fuel expansion; no general rejection of growth is inferred. Culture, ecology, technology, globalism and remaining null statements were checked against the downloaded full texts; general modernization and AI discussion do not establish technological determinism or algorithmic rule.
